exam.title: ServiceNow Certified Application Developer
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite is published. ServiceNow recommends application-development and system-administration experience, JavaScript/web-development fundamentals, and developer access in a nonproduction instance. Practice a complete scoped-application lifecycle across fit and data model, interfaces, ACL/cross-scope security, declarative and scripted automation, import/REST integration, source review, delegated development, testing, promotion and rollback.

review.notes: All six January 2026 evidence-baseline domains remain mapped through a complete scoped-application lifecycle: fit and data model, persona-tested interfaces, layered ACL/module/cross-scope security, declarative and scripted automation, reconciled import/REST integration, and reviewed source/repository/delegated-development promotion and rollback. Three integrated scenarios, eight authorized nonproduction labs and 40 original checks are included. KB0011498 still exposes only its title to deterministic and indexed extraction, so the current detailed objective and contract audit remains freshness-blocked. Current official planning documentation and a ServiceNow employee-authored ACL article add practice context; a May community discussion is explicitly non-authoritative. The official MeasureUp bank's displayed 20/20/20/20/10/10 distribution remains separated from the September 2 mainline evidence baseline of 15/20/20/20/10/15. Only MeasureUp is named for exam-style practice; no recalled/live item, dump or copied course content is used. September 17, 2026 maintenance: recovered the public CAD blueprint in an unsigned browser; corrected domain 1 to 20% and domain 6 to 10%, reconciled the practice-bank discrepancy, and confirmed the public exam contract. Historical review date and snapshot remain unchanged; see docs/research/2026-09-17-exam-validation.md.

findings.title: Field access does not repair missing table authorization
findings.evidence: Community junior/senior example omits a qualifying table grant or inheritance; primary reference requires applicable table and field access.
findings.recommendation: Teach separate table/field requirements and original negative cases; do not accept the community example as runtime proof.
findings.resolution: Teach separate table/field requirements and original negative cases; do not accept the community example as runtime proof.

findings.title: Standard secure record access is not automatic query-ACL opt-in
findings.evidence: Primary API sections distinguish standard CRUD ACL enforcement from explicitly enabled query ACLs and trusted/untrusted query methods.
findings.recommendation: Separate query and output authorization, require a narrow structured contract and verify installed API availability.
findings.resolution: Separate query and output authorization, require a narrow structured contract and verify installed API availability.

findings.title: REST query and pagination behavior need explicit failure handling
findings.evidence: Limit is applied before ACL filtering; invalid query portions can be dropped; cross-scope CRUD switches do not govern web-service requests.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish REST and script gates; teach validated input and endpoint-specific continuation despite an empty page, with bounded local counterexamples.
findings.resolution: Distinguish REST and script gates; teach validated input and endpoint-specific continuation despite an empty page, with bounded local counterexamples.

findings.title: Source-control history does not prove safe deployment or individual credential isolation
findings.evidence: Reference limits management to nonproduction, describes shared repository credentials and sanitization for unsupported external edits.
findings.recommendation: Separate metadata history, credential scope, supported editing and actual installed-state/promotion evidence.
findings.resolution: Separate metadata history, credential scope, supported editing and actual installed-state/promotion evidence.

findings.title: Test fixtures and custom UI retrieval require explicit isolation and transport checks
findings.evidence: Reference recommends isolated test-created users/records and documents custom UI component retrieval limits.
findings.recommendation: Require nonproduction fixtures, allowed/denied outcomes and target-environment component verification; do not imply local models executed ATF.
findings.resolution: Require nonproduction fixtures, allowed/denied outcomes and target-environment component verification; do not imply local models executed ATF.

findings.title: No-Allow-If behavior is contradictory in the primary page
findings.evidence: Pass row both requires explicit Allow-If and describes default grant when none exists.
findings.recommendation: Keep the support limitation visible pending authoritative evidence.
